question: I want to pull visitor counts per page for the last 30 days into my own dashboard. what do i send to the API and how do i authenticate?
reference_answer: Send a POST request to https://plausible.io/api/v2/query with an Authorization: Bearer header holding your Stats API key. In the JSON body, set your site_id, metrics ["visitors"], date_range "30d" and dimensions ["event:page"] to group visitors by page.
answer: To pull visitor counts per page, you can use the Stats API by sending a POST request to the `/api/v2/query` endpoint [1]. You must authenticate your request by including your Stats API key in the Authorization header using the Bearer Token method [1][2]. To get the data, send a JSON body containing your `site_id`, the `visitors` metric, and a `30d` date range [1][2].

evidence.title: Plausible Stats API reference
evidence.text:
Plausible Stats API is a read-only HTTP interface for **viewing historical and real-time stats**. The `/api/v2/query` endpoint accepts simple and complex stats queries in the POST request body and returns the metrics as JSON.

Tip: Not what you need?
Take a look at our Events API Reference if you want to record pageviews or custom events for your sites, or Sites API Reference if you want to manage your sites over the API.

## Authentication

API keys are scoped to one team. The team selected in the top-right menu when you create the key determines which sites it can query. A key does not inherit access to every site its owner can view across Plausible.

To create a Stats API key:

1. Log in to your Plausible account and select the team whose sites you want to query.
2. Click your account name, open the settings and go to **API Keys**.
3. Click **New API Key**, choose **Stats API** and save the key because it will only be shown once.
4. Click **Create API Key** to confirm its creation.

After creating an API key, you can authenticate your request by sending the key in the Authorization header of your request.

### Who can create a Stats API key?

| Role in the selected team | Can create a key for that team? |
| --- | --- |
| Owner, Admin, Editor or Billing | Yes |
| Viewer | No |
| Guest Viewer or Guest Editor for an individual site | No |

evidence.title: Plausible Stats API reference
evidence.text:
In the following request, replace `YOUR-KEY` with a reference to your stats API key and `site_id` value with your domain as you've added it to your Plausible account.

```bash
curl \
--request POST \
# highlight-next-line
--header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR-KEY' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--url 'https://plausible.io/api/v2/query' \
--data '{ "site_id": "dummy.site", "metrics": ["visitors"], "date_range": "7d" }'
```

The Stats API has a rate limit of 600 requests per hour by default. If you have special needs for more requests, please contact us to request more capacity.

evidence.title: Troubleshooting Plausible Analytics
evidence.text:
Some visitors use tools that block analytics scripts: browser extensions, privacy-focused browsers, Pi-hole and other network-level blockers, and corporate firewalls.

You have two options:

**Accept that some visitors won't be counted.** For most sites this is a small share of traffic. Plausible is blocked less than most analytics tools. Firefox and Safari have built-in tracking protection that blocks Google Analytics but not Plausible.

**Set up a proxy.** A proxy serves the Plausible script as a first-party request from your own domain, bypassing most blockers:

- The WordPress plugin has a one-click proxy built in
- Self-setup guides for Cloudflare, Netlify, Vercel and other platforms
- A managed proxy where we handle the setup for you. See proxy introduction for details

### Are some VPN visitors being filtered as bots?

Some VPN and iCloud Private Relay IP ranges overlap with data centers, so those visits are filtered with bot traffic. See VPN users and bot filtering.

evidence.title: Bypass adblockers with a proxy
evidence.text:
Some visitors use adblockers or privacy tools that block analytics scripts. Plausible is blocked far less than Google Analytics. Firefox and Safari do not block it by default, but some blocklist maintainers block all analytics regardless of privacy practices.

A proxy routes the Plausible script through your own domain as a first-party request, making it indistinguishable from your own files. This bypasses most blockers and lets you count visits that would otherwise be missed.

### No proxy (default)

Run the default script from plausible.io. This is the simplest setup and works well for most sites. Expect some visitors with strict blockers to be missed, typically between 5% and 25% depending on your audience.

**Use this when:** accuracy gaps from adblockers are acceptable for your use case.

### WordPress one-click proxy

The official WordPress plugin includes a built-in proxy you can enable with a single toggle in your plugin settings. No CNAME records, no server configuration, no maintenance.

**Use this when:** your site runs on WordPress.

WordPress plugin →

### Self-setup proxy

Route requests through your own infrastructure using a Cloudflare Worker, Vercel rewrite, Netlify redirect or reverse proxy. Requires developer access but is free and gives you full control.

**Use this when:** you are not on WordPress, have developer access, and want to manage the proxy yourself.

Using the NPM package? The tracker is already part of your own code, so you only need to proxy the event endpoint and set `endpoint` in `init`.

question: i did a csv import and now it says Dates Conflict even for months where my dashboard is empty. i had a gap in the middle where the script wasnt installed. can i fill it?
reference_answer: An import can't fill a gap that comes after your first Plausible data, which is why you see Dates Conflict. To fill such a gap, export your stats, reset your site's stats and import everything again: the exported files plus the data for the gap.
key_facts: Imports can't fill gaps after the first native Plausible data
Workaround: export stats, reset site stats, then import everything again
The gap data can be in CSV files too
answer: To fill a gap that occurs after your first Plausible data, you can export your stats, reset your site's stats, and then import everything again, including the exported files and the data for the gap [1]. This method works when the data for the gap is also in CSV files [1].

citations.quote: To fill such a gap, you can export your stats, reset your site's stats and import everything again, the exported files and the data for the gap. This works when the data for the gap is in CSV files too.

evidence.title: Import stats using CSV files
evidence.text:
Data is imported in aggregate for each date, from your first import visitor until your first Plausible Analytics visitor. This is to avoid double-counting visits. We also have measures in place to detect and avoid double-counting visitors if you import multiple properties into the same Plausible dashboard.

This means an import can't fill a gap that comes after your first Plausible data, such as months when the script wasn't installed between two periods of native stats. The import page then shows **Dates Conflict**, even for dates where your dashboard shows no visits. To fill such a gap, you can export your stats, reset your site's stats and import everything again, the exported files and the data for the gap. This works when the data for the gap is in CSV files too. A Google Analytics import picks the longest stretch of dates that no other import covers, so it can't be aimed at just the gap. Your native stats then become imported data, with the differences described below.

evidence.title: Plausible Events API reference
evidence.text:
The API always returns HTTP 202 Accepted, even when an event is dropped. To debug your setup, there are two tools:

**Check if events are being dropped:** Inspect the response headers for `x-plausible-dropped: 1`. When present, the event was rejected by bot filtering. The most common cause is `X-Forwarded-For` containing a server or CDN IP instead of the actual visitor IP.

**Check which IP address Plausible sees:** Add the `X-Debug-Request: true` header to your request. The API will return HTTP 200 with the IP address it will use for unique visitor counting. Use this to confirm that `X-Forwarded-For` is being forwarded correctly from your proxy. Requests sent with this header are not recorded in your stats, so use it on separate test requests rather than on your real events.

E.g: Add this header to your request and log the response.

**Test the path your real events take.** Send an `X-Debug-Request` test request from the same place your production events are sent (your server, worker, edge function or retry job), not only from your own computer. `X-Forwarded-For` can be set correctly in your code and still reach us with a different IP: a proxy, CDN, load balancer or hosting provider along the way may replace the header or add its own address to it. If the header contains a comma-separated list, Plausible uses the first valid IP address in it, so make sure the visitor's IP comes first. Also check that the visitor's original `User-Agent` is forwarded, not your server's or HTTP library's default.

Dropped events can't be added to your stats afterwards, so it's worth running these checks whenever you set up or change your integration.

Our 15% discount is available only to nonprofits, educational institutions and open-source projects choosing a Business plan with annual billing.

## What's included

The discount is 15% off a Business plan with annual billing. Combined with annual billing, you also get 2 months free.

The discount applies to new subscriptions to Business plans with annual billing only. Existing subscriptions, monthly payments and all other plans are excluded.

Your discount continues on renewals for as long as you stay on the same plan. If you upgrade or downgrade your plan for any reason, the discount ends and regular prices apply to your new plan.

## How to apply

1. Start your free 30-day trial. No credit card required.
2. Choose the Business pageview tier you need with annual billing.
3. If you meet the eligibility requirements below and are choosing a Business plan with annual billing, contact us with your organization or project name, type, website and preferred Business pageview tier.
4. We'll send you a discount code to use at checkout.

## Who qualifies

Only nonprofits, educational institutions and open-source projects qualify for this discount. If your organization or project does not fall into one of these categories, it is not eligible.

Plausible and Paddle use separate email addresses. Your Plausible email is for logging in and viewing your stats. Your Paddle email is where invoices are sent.

## Change your invoice email

If you want invoices sent to a different address, contact us with your current Paddle email and the new address you'd like to use. We'll update it with Paddle on your behalf.

To change your Plausible login email instead, see change your account email.

## Give your accounting team billing access

You can add a team member with the Billing role. A Billing member can view all past invoices, save them as PDFs and manage your subscription and payment details directly within Plausible.

To add a billing member, go to your team settings and invite them with the Billing role. See users and roles for details.
